title: Equivalent Fractions and Reducing Fractions to Simplest Form
seo_title: Grade 4 Equivalent Fractions Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Generate equivalent fractions using models; determine equivalent fractions; reduce fractions to simplest form.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 equivalent fractions worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: models, multiplying and dividing, simplest form and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equivalent fractions name the same amount, like 12 = 24 = 48.
  • Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
  • A fraction is in simplest form when 1 is the only number that divides both the numerator and the denominator.
  • To reduce, divide both by their greatest common factor. You can also divide in small steps until you cannot go on.

Examples

Example

1824 in simplest form

18 ÷ 6 = 3

24 ÷ 6 = 4

Answer: 34

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the same number12 is not 23. Multiply instead.
Changing only one numberDo the same to the top and the bottom.
Stopping too soon68 can still be reduced to 34.

items.q: The bar shows 68. The thick lines put the parts into groups of 2. What is 68 in simplest form?
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded. 6 and 8 can both be divided by 2. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 1 is the only number that divides both 3 and 4, so 34 is in simplest form. 68 = 34.

items.q: Christian ate 24 of a pizza. Rodel ate 48 of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom of 24 by 2: 24 = 48. Rodel ate more slices, but they were smaller, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Jasmine eats 2 slices. Which fraction also names how much she ate?

items.q: A pan of brownies is cut into 12 equal pieces. Gabriel eats 4 of them. What fraction of the pan is that, in thirds?
items.e: 412 = 13: divide the top and bottom by 4 (12 ÷ 4 = 3). Four twelfths fill one third.
